_schema.sizing: base_ram_gb / base_vcpu / base_disk_gb describe the whole stack at rest, including the database and any sidecar containers the project ships in its reference compose file. The per_user figures are the marginal cost of one additional active user.
_schema.sizing_basis: vendor_docs = the base figures come from the project's own documented minimum or recommended requirements. estimate = derived from the shipped compose stack and comparable deployments, and labelled as an estimate on the page.
_schema.difficulty: easy = single container, no external dependencies, no scheduled maintenance beyond image updates. medium = multi-container stack with a database to back up. hard = several stateful services, non-trivial upgrade path, or a real risk of data loss during upgrades.
_schema.replaces: Slugs from saas.json. Drives which comparison pages get generated.

tools.name: Vaultwarden
tools.sizing_note: A Rust reimplementation of the Bitwarden server. It runs comfortably in a fraction of a gigabyte because vault data is small and encrypted client-side.
tools.compatible_clients: Official Bitwarden mobile, desktop and browser clients point at it unchanged.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: Unofficial Bitwarden compatible server written in Rust, formerly known as bitwarden_rs

tools.name: Passbolt
tools.sizing_note: PHP application with MariaDB. GPG key handling makes onboarding slower than Vaultwarden but the audit trail is stronger.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: Passbolt Community Edition (CE) API. The JSON API for the open source password manager for teams!

tools.name: Plausible Analytics
tools.sizing_note: Ships as Elixir plus ClickHouse plus PostgreSQL. ClickHouse sets the memory floor, so this stack does not usefully shrink below 2 GB. Disk scales with pageviews rather than with seats.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: Open source, privacy-first web analytics. Lightweight, cookie-free Google Analytics alternative. Self-hosted or cloud.

tools.name: Umami
tools.sizing_note: Next.js application against PostgreSQL or MySQL. The lightest credible analytics stack: two containers and no separate column store.
tools.description_gh: Umami is a privacy-first analytics platform. Traffic, campaigns, behavior, conversions, and revenue in one place — no cookies, no surveillance, self-hosted or in the cloud.

tools.name: Matomo
tools.sizing_note: The most feature-complete option and the heaviest. Report archiving is the expensive part and wants a cron job with real memory behind it.
tools.description_gh: Empowering People Ethically 🚀 — Matomo is hiring! Join us → https://matomo.org/jobs Matomo is the leading open-source alternative to Google Analytics, giving you complete control and built-in privacy. Easily collect, visualise, and analyse data from websites & apps. Star us on GitHub ⭐️  – Pull Requests welcome!

tools.name: PostHog
tools.sizing_note: Kafka, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, Redis and several workers. PostHog itself now discourages self-hosting below a substantial scale, and the sizing here reflects that honestly.
tools.description_gh: :hedgehog: PostHog is the leading platform for building self-driving products. Our developer tools – AI observability, analytics, session replay, flags, experiments, error tracking, logs, and more – capture all the context agents need to diagnose problems, uncover opportunities, and ship fixes. Steer it all from Slack, web, desktop, or the MCP.

tools.name: n8n
tools.sizing_note: The base figure covers a single main process with SQLite. Heavy workflow volume wants PostgreSQL and queue mode with separate workers, which roughly doubles the floor.
tools.licence_caveat: Source-available under the Sustainable Use Licence, not a classic open-source licence. Internal business use is permitted; reselling n8n as a service is not.
tools.description_gh: Fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities. Combine visual building with custom code, self-host or cloud, 400+ integrations.

tools.name: Activepieces
tools.sizing_note: Application, PostgreSQL and Redis. Isolated sandboxes for code steps are what push the memory floor above n8n's.
tools.description_gh: AI Agents & MCPs & AI Workflow Automation • (~400 MCP servers for AI agents) • AI Automation / AI Agent with MCPs • AI Workflows & AI Agents • MCPs for AI Agents

tools.name: Windmill
tools.sizing_note: Rust server with PostgreSQL and one or more workers. Faster per job than the Node-based options, which matters if the workflow count is high.
tools.description_gh: Open-source developer platform to power your entire infra and turn scripts into webhooks, workflows and UIs. Fastest workflow engine (13x vs Airflow). Open-source alternative to Retool and Temporal.

tools.name: Outline
tools.sizing_note: Needs PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible object storage for attachments. The object storage requirement is the part people miss when budgeting.
tools.description_gh: The fastest knowledge base for growing teams. Beautiful, realtime collaborative, feature packed, and markdown compatible.

tools.name: Docmost
tools.sizing_note: PostgreSQL and Redis, with local disk for attachments by default. Closest to Confluence's page-tree model of the current crop.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: Docmost is an open-source collaborative wiki and documentation software. It is an open-source alternative to Confluence and Notion.

tools.name: BookStack
tools.sizing_note: Laravel and MySQL. The least demanding wiki on this list and the easiest to back up, because it is one database and one uploads directory.
tools.description_gh: NOW MANAGED ON CODEBERG

tools.name: AFFiNE
tools.sizing_note: The closest match to Notion's block editor and whiteboard combination. Self-hosting is supported but moves faster than the other options here, so pin your image tag.
tools.description_gh: There can be more than Notion and Miro. AFFiNE(pronounced [ə‘fain]) is a next-gen knowledge base that brings planning, sorting and creating all together. Privacy first, open-source, customizable and ready to use.

tools.name: Plane
tools.sizing_note: Django API, web and space frontends, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ and MinIO. A genuine Jira substitute and priced like one in RAM terms.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: 🔥🔥🔥 Open-source Jira, Linear, Monday, and ClickUp alternative. Plane is a modern project management platform to manage tasks, sprints, docs, and triage.

tools.name: Vikunja
tools.sizing_note: A single Go binary with SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL. Kanban, list and Gantt views without the operational weight of Plane.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: The task manager you actually own.

tools.name: OpenProject
tools.sizing_note: Rails monolith with PostgreSQL and Memcached. Carries classical project management, including baselines and earned value, which the newer tools omit.
tools.description_gh: OpenProject is the leading open source project management software for product, project and portfolio management. A powerful Jira alternative with agile planning, issue tracking, roadmaps, Gantt charts, time tracking, collaboration features, and more. Available on premises or in the cloud. ⭐ Star us on GitHub

tools.name: Chatwoot
tools.sizing_note: Rails web process plus a Sidekiq worker, PostgreSQL and Redis. The worker is not optional; skipping it silently breaks outbound email and webhooks.
tools.description_gh: Open-source live-chat, email support, omni-channel desk. An alternative to Intercom, Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud etc. 🔥💬

tools.name: FreeScout
tools.sizing_note: Laravel and MySQL. A shared mailbox rather than a full support suite, which is exactly what most small teams are overpaying Zendesk for.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: FreeScout — Free self-hosted omnichannel AI-powered helpdesk & shared mailbox

tools.name: Zammad
tools.sizing_note: Rails with PostgreSQL, Redis and Elasticsearch. Elasticsearch is what makes this the heaviest helpdesk here, and it is effectively required for usable search.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: Zammad is a web based open source helpdesk/customer support system.

tools.name: Keycloak
tools.sizing_note: JVM service with PostgreSQL. Memory is dominated by the heap rather than by user count, so cost per user falls steeply as the directory grows. This is the CNCF-backed incumbent.
tools.description_gh: Open Source Identity and Access Management For Modern Applications and Services

tools.name: authentik
tools.sizing_note: Server plus worker, PostgreSQL and Redis. Friendlier than Keycloak for proxy-style protection of apps that have no native SSO support.
tools.description_gh: The authentication glue you need.

tools.name: Zitadel
tools.sizing_note: Go binary over PostgreSQL, with an event-sourced audit log. Lighter than the JVM option and closer to Auth0's developer ergonomics.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: ZITADEL - Identity infrastructure, simplified for you.

tools.name: Uptime Kuma
tools.sizing_note: One container with SQLite. Cost scales with the number of monitors and their check interval, not with the number of people reading the dashboard.
tools.description_gh: A fancy self-hosted monitoring tool

tools.name: Gatus
tools.sizing_note: Configuration as YAML in version control, which suits teams that want their monitoring reviewed like code. The smallest footprint on this entire site.
tools.description_gh: Automated developer-oriented status page with alerting and incident support

tools.name: Metabase
tools.sizing_note: JVM application with an application database of its own. Concurrent query load, not seat count, is what forces an upgrade here.
tools.description_gh: The easy-to-use open source Business Intelligence and Embedded Analytics tool that lets everyone work with data :bar_chart:

tools.name: Apache Superset
tools.sizing_note: Web process, Celery workers, beat scheduler, PostgreSQL and Redis. More capable than Metabase and considerably more to operate.
tools.description_gh: Apache Superset is a Data Visualization and Data Exploration Platform

tools.name: Lightdash
tools.sizing_note: Builds on dbt metrics, so it only makes sense if a dbt project already exists. Where it does, the modelling work is already paid for.
tools.description_gh: Agentic BI. Analytics at the speed of code ⚡️

tools.name: Formbricks
tools.sizing_note: Next.js with PostgreSQL. Aimed at in-product surveys as much as standalone forms, which is where Typeform's per-response pricing bites hardest.
tools.description_gh: Open Source Qualtrics Alternative

tools.name: OpnForm
tools.sizing_note: Laravel and Vue over PostgreSQL. The most direct Typeform substitute for plain form building.
tools.description_gh: Beautiful Open-Source Form Builder

tools.name: LimeSurvey
tools.sizing_note: Two decades of survey logic, including quotas and complex branching that the newer tools do not attempt. The interface shows its age.
tools.description_gh: 🔥 LimeSurvey – A powerful, open-source survey platform. A free alternative to SurveyMonkey, Typeform, Qualtrics, and Google Forms, making it simple to create online surveys and forms with unmatched flexibility.

tools.name: Nextcloud
tools.sizing_note: Disk per user is the line that decides this comparison, not RAM. At 15 GB a head, storage overtakes compute well before 50 users.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: ☁️ Nextcloud server, a safe home for all your data

tools.name: Seafile
tools.sizing_note: Block-level sync makes it noticeably faster than Nextcloud on large files, at the cost of a much smaller app ecosystem.
tools.description_gh: Beyond file syncing and sharing, a new way to organize your files with extensible file properties and flexible views

tools.name: Mattermost
tools.sizing_note: Go server with PostgreSQL. Unlimited searchable history is the whole point: Slack's free tier hides the archive, and that is what pushes teams onto a paid plan.
tools.description_gh: Mattermost is an open source platform for secure collaboration across the entire software development lifecycle..

tools.name: Zulip
tools.sizing_note: Django with PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ and memcached. The topic-threaded model is genuinely better for asynchronous work than Slack's channels.
tools.description_gh: Zulip server and web application. Open-source team chat that helps teams stay productive and focused.

tools.name: Rocket.Chat
tools.sizing_note: Node with MongoDB. The MongoDB replica-set requirement is the part that surprises people during the first upgrade.
tools.description_gh: The Secure CommsOS™ for mission-critical operations

tools.name: Listmonk
tools.sizing_note: Single Go binary with PostgreSQL. It does not send mail itself: budget for an SMTP relay separately, which is where the real per-message cost sits.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: High performance, self-hosted, newsletter and mailing list manager with a modern dashboard. Single binary app.

tools.name: Mautic
tools.sizing_note: Full marketing automation with campaign branching and lead scoring. The cron-driven architecture is the main operational burden.
tools.description_gh: Mautic: Open Source Marketing Automation Software.

tools.name: Twenty
tools.sizing_note: Server, worker, PostgreSQL and Redis. The most credible modern-feeling open CRM, and still moving fast enough that you should pin versions.
tools.description_gh: The open alternative to Salesforce, designed for AI.

tools.name: EspoCRM
tools.sizing_note: PHP and MySQL, and by far the cheapest way to run a real CRM. Less polished than Twenty but stable and easy to back up.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: EspoCRM – Open Source CRM Application

tools.name: DocuSeal
tools.sizing_note: One container and a database. Removes DocuSign's per-envelope charge, which is the line item that makes signature tools expensive.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: Open source DocuSign alternative. Create, fill, and sign digital documents ✍️

tools.name: Documenso
tools.sizing_note: Next.js with PostgreSQL and real certificate-based signing, which matters if the signatures have to stand up legally.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: The Open Source DocuSign Alternative.

tools.name: GlitchTip
tools.sizing_note: Sentry-SDK compatible, so existing client instrumentation keeps working unchanged. Far lighter than self-hosted Sentry, which needs Kafka and ClickHouse. Source lives on GitLab rather than GitHub, so the star count shown elsewhere on this site is not available for it.

tools.name: SigNoz
tools.sizing_note: OpenTelemetry-native traces, metrics and logs over ClickHouse. Replaces a Datadog bill rather than just a Sentry bill, and the retention window drives the disk cost.
tools.description_gh: SigNoz is an open-source, OpenTelemetry-native observability platform for your team and their AI agents. Get logs, metrics, and traces in one tool with features like APM, distributed tracing, log management, infra monitoring, etc. Combined with SigNoz MCP and a native AI teammate (in SigNoz Cloud) it helps you build more resilient apps.

tools.name: Cal.com
tools.sizing_note: Next.js with PostgreSQL. A close feature match for Calendly; the calendar OAuth setup is the fiddly part of the install.
tools.licence_caveat: AGPL-3.0 core with some enterprise features under a separate commercial licence.
tools.description_gh: Scheduling infrastructure for absolutely everyone.

tools.name: Immich
tools.sizing_note: Server, machine-learning container, PostgreSQL with pgvector, and Redis. The ML container is what sets the 4 GB floor, and photo storage dominates the total cost.
tools.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
tools.description_gh: High performance self-hosted photo and video management solution.

tools.name: PhotoPrism
tools.sizing_note: Go with MariaDB and on-device classification. Lighter than Immich but its multi-user story is weaker.
tools.description_gh: AI-Powered Photos App 🌈💎✨
